evidence: Vulg. 1 Cor. 15.57: Deō autem grātiās, quī dedit nōbīs victōriam
Vulg. 2 Cor. 9.15: Grātiās Deō super inēnarrābilī dōnō ejus.
terms.comment: The Christian form, from Paul’s letters; the household’s word.

evidence: Traupman 121: Sit dīs grātia, thank heaven
terms.comment: The classical (pagan) phrase; dīs grātiam habeō, “I thank the gods”, in full.

terms.register: superī: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor., Ov.
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase; Lewis & Short does not quote it. Superī, the gods above, is mostly poetic; comedy says Dīs grātia.

phrases.latin: Deō autem grātiās, quī dedit nōbīs victōriam per Dominum nostrum Jēsum Chrīstum.
phrases.english: But thanks be to God, who has given us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

phrases.latin: Quid ais? an vēnit Pamphilus? — Vēnit. — Dīs grātiam habeō.
phrases.english: What are you saying? Has Pamphilus come? — He has. — Thank God.

phrases.latin: Dī mē servant, salva rēs est.
phrases.english: The gods are keeping me safe; all’s well.

sources: Lewis & Short: gratia · Lewis & Short: deus
